name: Illinois
nameStory: A French spelling of the Illinois people's own name, which meant roughly 'those who speak the ordinary way.' The French added an '-ois' ending, and that is why there is an 's' on the end that nobody pronounces.
capitalStory: Springfield became the capital because of nine lobbying legislators nicknamed the 'Long Nine' - all of them over six feet tall, including a young Abraham Lincoln. He then lived there for 24 years, longer than anywhere else.
funFacts: Cahokia, near modern St. Louis, was the largest city north of Mexico before Columbus - bigger at its peak than London was at the time.
Chicago built the world's first steel-frame skyscraper in 1885.
In 1900 engineers reversed the flow of the Chicago River so the city's sewage would go toward the Mississippi instead of its own drinking water.
The highest point in Illinois is only 1,235 feet.
